name: Javad Mahjoub
event: UFC Fight Night: Buckley vs. Malott
summary: A 35-year-old Iranian-born heavyweight (5-0) and two-time Olympic judoka (Rio 2016 for Iran, Tokyo 2020 on the Refugee Olympic Team, 2013 Asian champion at -100 kg) who turned to MMA in 2022. Four of his five wins ended in round one; he makes his UFC debut against fellow newcomer Joel Faglier after Louie Sutherland withdrew.

how_they_fight.Striking: Three first-round TKOs (Navarrete 1:45, Patry 0:55 on a knee injury, Duarte 2:07), but against modest regional opposition; little film or stat detail exists.
how_they_fight.Grappling: Elite judo base: throws, top control and finishing from top. Submitted Pietro Gentile with an armbar at 4:59 of round one in February 2026.
how_they_fight.Defense: Never stopped or dropped a decision; only one fight (WXF, Seoul, 2025, three 4-minute rounds) went the distance. Unknown how he handles heavyweight power over time.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: A first-round finisher: 4 of 5 wins in R1 and the other a 12-minute decision over Gamzat Sirazhudinov. Never been past the 12-minute mark; at 35 with only ~22 minutes of pro cage time, cardio over 15 minutes is unproven.
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Decades of elite competition experience in judo, but only five pro MMA fights, with long gaps (Aug 2023 to Sep 2025).

patterns: Ends fights early: 4 of 5 wins in round one
Mix of ground strikes and submissions after getting on top
One decision win, over three 4-minute rounds
concerns: Age 35 with thin MMA experience and a two-year gap in 2023-2025
Opponent changed from Louie Sutherland to Joel Faglier about two and a half weeks out
Team listings disagree: our data has Alavanca Calgary; Wikipedia lists Tristar Gym in Montreal
keys_to_beat: Avoid the clinch and upper-body ties where his judo works
Keep it at range and drag him into rounds 2 and 3
Make him strike for long stretches against a heavyweight with real power

news.text: Signed by the UFC as an undefeated (5-0) heavyweight prospect.
Louie Sutherland pulled out (no reason given); fellow newcomer Joel Faglier replaces him.
